pages.text: With bronze in my hands I stopped fearing the night, and so I finally looked up. The stars were wrong: too bright, too deliberate, as if someone had set them there to be read.

Some trees here have leaves like stained glass. Their seeds grow a flower called magebloom, and magebloom remembers magic. I spun it into fibre and fed it to an apparatus that hummed when I came near.
Others chose the stars instead: starlight gathered in wells, crystals that sing under the night sky. Some chose blood, which always asks a price. Every path led to the same thing: a key.
Not a key to a door. A key to a dusk. I threw it into a pool ringed with flowers, and the water caught a light that was not quite fire.
Forged from magic I earned, not found. The portal answers nothing else.
pages.title: Mark of the Ritual Age
